expected: At high redshift, metallicity relations can disagree because galaxies evolved, or because calibrations changed the measuring scale. If the relation genuinely evolved, that would be a fact about the enrichment history of young galaxies. But an apparent offset could instead be a fact about strong-line recipes, reference frames, or scale conversions rather than galaxies. How do we tell evolution from calibration? The absolute metallicity scale (y-int) varies up to 0.7 dex, depending on the calibration used. Kewley and Ellison reported disagreement among the measurement rulers; the interpretation remains disputed, and this video adopts no answer as its finding.
